key_insight: V-DUGKS reformulates continuum compressible flow simulation with vectorial distribution functions and second-order Hermite equilibria to improve stability, efficiency, and Prandtl-number control.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more robust and faster kinetic solver for compressible Navier–Stokes problems, making it attractive for shock, vortex, and multi-dimensional CFD applications.
method: Uses coupled mass, momentum, and total-energy distribution functions with separate relaxation for momentum and energy transport.
Truncates equilibrium distributions at second-order Hermite level and uses fourth-order Gauss-Hermite quadrature for exact moment recovery.
Applies a finite-volume DUGKS update with characteristic-based fluxes and trapezoidal collision integration.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports accurate results on shock-tube, Shu-Osher, 2D Riemann, and 3D Taylor-Green vortex tests, with about 2.2–2.9× speed-up in the 3D Taylor-Green case.
watch_item: Performance may depend on careful choice of discrete velocity sets, reference temperature, and CFL/time-step settings to preserve stability and accuracy.
paper_title: Vectorial discrete unified gas kinetic scheme for continuum compressible flows
